senses.definition: comparative form of strong: more strong

quotes.text: As a result, New Zealand locomotive design is a curious blend of English and American practice; certainly the American influence has always been much stronger than in Australia.
quotes.reference: 1954 August, J. B. Snell, “The New Zealand Government Railways—2”, in Railway Magazine, page 558:

senses.definition: (logic) Said of one proposition with respect to another one: that the former entails the latter, but the latter does not entail the former.

examples: Compared to the previous semester, my grades now are a lot stronger.
